item.title: Understand a switch to a daytime shift
item.summary: A supervisor gives a worker two options for a one-week change.
item.transcript_text:
Manager: From Monday, the late shift ends at eight instead of nine because the building work starts each evening. If you need your usual hours, you can either start at three or add the missing hour to Friday's morning shift.
Worker: I'm in class until half past three on Mondays and Wednesdays.
Manager: Then three won't work on those days. You could add one hour to Friday and one to Saturday. Check with Lynn before you do that. She keeps the weekend list.
Worker: Can I leave at nine again when the builders finish?
Manager: Yes. This change is only for next week. I'll put the normal hours back on the board the week after.

options: A class starting at the workplace
questions.explanation: The workers leave earlier because of the work on the building.

questions.prompt: Which days cause the worker a problem with a three o’clock start?
questions.explanation: Their class runs until 3:30 on Monday and Wednesday.

questions.prompt: What option does the manager suggest for recovering both hours?
options: Add one to Friday and one to Saturday
Work two extra hours on Monday
Add one to Wednesday and one to Friday
questions.explanation: The manager offers Friday and Saturday as the two make-up days.

questions.prompt: Who should be asked about that plan first?
When should normal late shifts return?
options: At the end of each day
The week after the temporary change
questions.explanation: The manager says the change is for one week.

children.segment_text: because the building work starts each evening
